verdicts.evidence: Self-adjointness error |⟨Af,g⟩−⟨f,Ag⟩| is ~1e-17 (dense graphon) and 2.22e-16 (sparse 4-regular graph as graphop), with zero positivity violations in both; mutation tests with antisymmetric and symmetric signed kernels independently break the two properties, confirming the probes are not cross-contaminated.

Sweep over n∈{100,200,400,800,1600} shows fiber sup stays constant at 4 (exponent ≈0, |slope|<0.05) for bounded-degree graphs, while dense ER p=0.3 grows with exponent 0.947 and a single √n hub grows with exponent 0.413, demonstrating the condition discriminates sparse from unbounded connectivity.

With n=200, r=4, D=3, tanh layer, the theoretical bound C_theory=20.5 is not exceeded by empirical ratios (4.195 for signal-only perturbation, 0.157 for joint perturbation), computed using exact SVD for the operator term; dense ER mutation gives ratio 94.63>20.5, confirming the fiber bound is necessary for finiteness.

Greedy ε-net over N∈{10,20,40} sampled DIDMs shows saturation for bofops (2/3/3 net points) but not for unbounded fibers (9/19/35), and a dense-graph DIDM sits at W₁ distance 66.85 from all bofop-DIDMs; however, a finite ε-net is explicitly acknowledged as a surrogate for the infinite-dimensional compactness statement.

Random-feature MPNN with widths 8→256 on 220 train/120 test bofop graphs shows sup-norm error decreasing from 0.0516 to 0.0068 for a continuous DIDM target, while a discontinuous target plateaus at ~0.5–0.6; this is a finite-width, finite-sample proxy for the asymptotic universal approximation theorem.

Training-size sweep m∈{25,50,100,200,400} with 6 replicates shows bofop generalization gap decreasing from 2.78e-3 to 2.23e-4 (log-log slope −0.871), but the non-bofop mutation also vanishes (slope −1.350) and the experiment is a finite-m surrogate for the asymptotic bound; the caveat that compactness is not isolated as strictly necessary for the rate is honestly retained.

overall: The logbook provides machine-precision numerical verification for the three definitional/finite-level claims (1–3) through exact computations and well-designed mutation tests. Claims 4–6 are addressed with real experiments and honest caveats, but remain finite surrogates for infinite-dimensional topological or asymptotic statements, placing them at the toy level.
